# Hybrid matching development set

`hybrid_dev_v1.json` freezes 48 ingredient descriptions in eight groups, six cases
per group: egg identity, cooking scope, meat, products, dairy, preservation,
portion handling and uncertainty. It includes 79 selected extraction-field checks,
48 candidate contrast checks and six known-description retrieval anchors.

All descriptions/expected labels are assistant-authored provisional development
material. They are not independently reviewed, a representative sample, a held-out
test set, or approved composition matches. Some deliberately reuse prior development
examples. Related wording belongs in the same development group; no generalization
claim is possible from tuning on this set.

The main fixture was frozen before implementing the hybrid module. Do not silently
edit its labels to improve scores: create a new dataset version with a change log.
Its SHA-256 is checked in `tests/test_hybrid_matching.py`:
`c65bc9dc5eee6919e863f2b218e507d9b78bc2ea9c8946aedac201d4b44b42dd`.

`hybrid_dev_v1_events.json` supplements the same cases with nine development checks
for modifier targets, quoted wording and polarity. It was authored during
development and is explicitly not held out. It leaves the original fixture intact.

## What expectations mean

- `expected`: selected extraction assertions only. Null explicitly checks that a
  fact is not asserted; omitted fields are unchecked, not negative labels.
- `compatibility_checks`: manually specified candidate-text contrasts, independent
  of which records vector retrieval happens to return. `compatible_proposal`
  denotes agreement under the provisional pilot policy, never production acceptance.
- `retrieval_anchor_label`: a known literal catalogue description to diagnose
  retrieval wiring. It is not an adjudicated acceptable nutritional target.
- Numeric scores from these checks measure development agreement. Full extraction
  precision, acceptable-record recall and nutritional accuracy are not established.

The independent-review CSV generated by the runner omits expected labels and
predicted choices. An independent reviewer can correct food/properties and assess
candidate source records there. Source nutrient basis/eligibility requires a
separate inspection. Keep the earlier 100-description blank review pack untouched.

## Run locally

Requires the existing offline catalogue, FoodOn dictionary/parent snapshot and
cached FEAST encoder. No training or provider calls.

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1 \
PYTHONPATH=src:. .venv/bin/python -m scripts.composition.evaluate_hybrid_dev \
  --output-dir /tmp/hybrid-dev-new

PYTHONPATH=src:. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_hybrid_matching.py -q
```

Use `--extraction-only` to skip embeddings/retrieval, or `--retrieval-file` with
a previous run's `retrieval.json` to hold candidate lists fixed while developing
policies. Output directories must be new. The maintained matching guide is
[docs/MATCHING.md](../../../docs/MATCHING.md); generated initial results are under
`analysis/hybrid_dev_2026-10-23_v3/`.

The subsequent vocabulary-backed implementation is summarized in that guide,
with its saved results in
`analysis/hybrid_dev_2026-10-23_vocabulary_v2/`. It leaves these frozen labels
unchanged; complete-case extraction quality still requires expanded independent labels.
